Predict from a quorum surrogate (mean + sd per output)

Source: R/surrogate.R
predict.fb_surrogate.Rd

Returns the surrogate's predictive distribution at new parameter sets. By default a data.frame carrying, for each emulated output <o>, a <o>_mean and a <o>_sd column. Reporting the predictive sd – not only the mean – is the contract-C7 distribution-preserving requirement.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'fb_surrogate'
predict(object, newdata, cov = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

object

An fb_surrogate from fit_surrogate().

newdata

A data.frame of new parameter sets; must contain the surrogate's param_names columns.

cov

FALSE (default) for the marginal data.frame; TRUE for an fb_surrogate_prediction with the dense per-row cross-output covariance array; "lowrank" for the compact factored covariance (a joint rff fit only).

...

Unused.

Value

With cov = FALSE (default) a data.frame with <output>_mean and <output>_sd columns, one row per row of newdata. With cov = TRUE an fb_surrogate_prediction (mean, cov, output_names). With cov = "lowrank" an fb_surrogate_prediction (mean, cov_lowrank, output_names).

Details

With cov = TRUE it returns the joint predictive distribution: an fb_surrogate_prediction carrying the predictive mean matrix and a per-row cross-output covariance array (contract C7 clause 4). A joint rff surrogate supplies the full covariance; a marginals-only surrogate (independent rff, or a conformer reporting only <o>_sd) returns a diagonal covariance built from the marginal sds, so the call always states its basis.

With cov = "lowrank" a joint rff surrogate returns the same joint predictive in a compact factored form for large output counts: an fb_surrogate_prediction carrying cov_lowrank = list(u, d, infl) such that per-row covariance is infl[i] * (u u' + diag(d)) – O(k q + n) storage instead of the dense O(k^2 n) array. The factor u has the surrogate's cov_rank columns (the full k if it was fit without cov_rank). Reconstruct a slice with fb_cov_slice(). The diagonal still equals <o>_sd^2 exactly.

For the reference rff method, writing \(\phi(x)\) for the random Fourier feature map of a new parameter set \(x\), the reported mean and variance are the Bayesian-linear-regression predictive moments $$ E[y \mid x] = \phi(x)^\top \mu_N, \qquad Var[y \mid x] = 1/t + \phi(x)^\top S_N \phi(x), $$ with posterior weight mean \(\mu_N\), posterior weight covariance \(S_N\), and noise precision \(t\) set by MacKay evidence maximisation at fit time (Bishop, 2006, sec. 3.3, 3.5).

References

Bishop, C. M. (2006). Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning. Springer, secs. 3.3 and 3.5.

Examples

theta <- cbind(p1 = runif(60, -2, 2), p2 = runif(60, -2, 2))
y <- theta %*% rbind(c(1.5, -0.8), c(0.4, 1.1)) + rnorm(120, 0, 0.1)
ens <- fb_ensemble(as.data.frame(theta), as.data.frame(y),
                    provenance = list(source = "raw"))
sur <- fit_surrogate(ens)
predict(sur, data.frame(p1 = 1, p2 = -1))
#>     V1_mean     V1_sd   V2_mean     V2_sd
#> V1 1.052805 0.1818922 -1.768903 0.1992059
